Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-lbveora1/call-769ec1c287b246c6abbbda9389bf5b84/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
for name in ('pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL'):
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
pdf=Path('manuscript.pdf')
print('pdf_bytes', pdf.stat().st_size)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    s=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    text.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+s)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant vision problem: maintaining minority-group accuracy under spurious correlations and distribution shift. SGDRO provides a simple, understandable combination of an average-loss SAM perturbation and group DRO updates, with explicit pseudocode.

Waterbirds results provide evidence of incremental benefit over GDRO under the same weight-decay setting. Across five seeds, worst-group accuracy increases from 86.5% to 87.2%, and both minority groups improve. Group-average accuracy also increases slightly, from 90.4% to 90.6%.

Evaluation covers six DomainBed datasets in addition to Waterbirds. SGDRO achieves 71.4% average accuracy versus 70.1% for GDRO and 70.9% for ERM, with three-seed results and training-domain validation for model selection.

Table 2 supports lower measured curvature relative to GDRO: both leading Hessian eigenvalues decrease for every group under matched weight decay. The largest pooled eigenvalue decreases from 356.6 to 268.7, providing useful evidence complementary to accuracy.
weaknesses: The central guarantees are unsupported. Section 3.1 supplies a local Taylor argument, without assumptions or a proof establishing common flat minima or worst-group generalization. Its displayed expansion also uses the overall-loss gradient and Hessian throughout; for a fixed active group, Equation 3 instead requires the group gradient plus the group Hessian applied to the normalized overall-loss gradient. Correcting this notation would still leave the substantive gap: a perturbation that increases average loss need not maximize any particular group's loss or control its sharpness.

The distinctive methodological choices are not isolated experimentally. There is no comparison against SAM applied directly to the GDRO objective, perturbations derived from group losses, or group-weight updates computed from unperturbed losses. SAM is also absent from the DomainBed comparison. Consequently, the experiments do not establish why the proposed coupling is preferable to straightforward alternatives built from the same components. This attribution gap substantially limits the supported originality.

The claimed alleviation of the average-versus-worst-group trade-off is not demonstrated. In Table 1, weighted average accuracy decreases from 93.8% for GDRO to 93.1% for SGDRO, and both majority groups lose accuracy. The result therefore shows additional minority-group gains accompanied by additional majority-group costs. Moreover, the worst-group gain is modest relative to the reported variability: 86.5 ± 0.7 versus 87.2 ± 0.5. The meaning of these Waterbirds error bars and uncertainty of the improvement are not specified.

The Hessian analysis supports a narrower conclusion than the manuscript draws. Test-loss eigenvalues and one-dimensional slices establish local curvature differences, but do not establish shared group minima or a causal explanation for generalization. Figure 2 also aligns curves by their minimum losses, preventing comparison of their absolute loss levels. No variability across seeds is reported for these diagnostics.

Reproducibility is partial despite the useful pseudocode and several stated hyperparameters. Backbone and pretraining details, stochastic group sampling, and the DomainBed perturbation-radius search range are not explicitly documented; references to earlier experimental settings leave ambiguity. These reporting issues are secondary. The unsupported central guarantees and lack of evidence isolating the proposed design choices determine the weak-reject recommendation, despite the worthwhile empirical gains.
